articles.title: “Race realism” isn’t realistic—and it isn’t good science
articles.description: Modern genetics does not support claims of innate racial differences in intelligence.
articles.content: At this year’s World Economic Forum meeting in Davos, US President Donald Trump stated that people from Somalia have low IQs. “I always say these are low-IQ people,” he said in his speech. His son, Donald Trump Jr, made a similar statement about Haitian people in 2024 (Trump’s government has since ended the protected status of both Somali and Haitian migrants in the US). These statements and their consequences are symptoms of a growing trend in Western politics: the re-emergence of racial views
articles.author: Jonathan R. Goodman and Rebecca Sear, The Conversation

articles.title: GLP-1 drugs could have a surprisingly large environmental payoff
articles.description: GLP-1 drugs could cut food demand enough to free farmland larger than Italy.
articles.content: GLP-1 weight-loss medicines such as Ozempic and Wegovy could affect much more than the waistlines of the people who take them. If widely used, our new research suggests these appetite-suppressing medicines could transform the global food system and free up vast areas of agricultural land. The global food system is ultimately driven by demand. If people eat less, producers respond, affecting production, prices, trade, and how much land is needed. We used a powerful computer simulation to explore
articles.author: Roslyn Henry and Peter Alexander, The Conversation
